_comment: Design tokens. scripts/gen_tokens.py emits DesignTokens.swift and mobile/src/generated/tokens.ts.
COLOUR SPACE IS LOAD-BEARING. SwiftUI's bare Color(red:green:blue:) is DISPLAY P3, while
react-native-svg takes sRGB hex. Using the bare initialiser would make the Mac card visibly
more saturated than the byte-identical phone card. The generated Swift always emits
Color(.sRGB, red:green:blue:opacity:). Every value below is sRGB.
The rules these values serve are in design-refs/DESIGN-DIRECTION.md section 3: one warm grey
family, three data hues that are never chrome, amber as the brand and the only action colour.
The owner lifted the one accent rule on 2026-09-13 (brief.md, 'Owner override': 'why are all
of them the same color?'). Identity now takes one of the nine `spectrum` hues below
(design-refs/DESIGN-V2-COLOUR-MOTION.md); the greys, the data hues and amber are unchanged.

strip._comment: Amber dominance = 'the agent was working'. Bone notches = you spoke. Teal = you typed code. The amber is the recognisable-at-a-glance colour, the way Strava's route is orange.

_comment: Depth on dark is a one-step lift plus a hairline: bg, then card, then raised, 1pt border.
textFaint is 3.2:1 on dark bg: disabled states and decoration only, never information.
Amber is spent on the primary fill, the active state, progress and 'needs you'. Amber TEXT
only at 13pt semibold or larger and only on dark (1.7:1 on the light bg).
Data hues: never chrome, never a fill behind text, never a chip. The third one, human
(teal), is strip.human_edit and is not repeated here so it cannot drift.
add is hue ~112, chosen far from the teal (~174) so the two never read as one colour.
del dark is the old DANGER; the light value exists because that red is 3.9:1 on white.

graph._comment: Contribution graph coloured by ACTIVE HOURS, not tokens. Buckets are ABSOLUTE (see Tuning.graphHourBuckets) so two profiles stay comparable — self-relative quantiles would make any shared screenshot meaningless. Amber ramp, deliberately not GitHub green.

_comment: System fonts only. No font files ship, so nothing to license and nothing to load.
SF Pro for words, SF Mono (design: monospaced) for machine data: repo names, model ids, paths.
size in points, weight 100-900, tracking in points, line as a multiple of size.
maxScale is the Dynamic Type ceiling: 1 means fixed. hero, display and label are fixed
because stat grids break (the Strava rule); body and meta scale with the reader.
Every number is tabular. One hero or display per screen. Nothing under 11pt.

cardType._comment: The share card export, in units of the 1600px export canvas, not phone points.

space._comment: 4pt base. The scale is 4 8 12 16 24 32 40 64 and nothing else. tile (12) is the gap between tiles and inside a container; section (32) is the gap between sections.

layout._comment: Named uses of the space scale. tilePad 14 is the one value off the scale, on purpose: it is the HIG margin for Live Activities, and the widget margin is 16.

radius._comment: Actions are capsules; containers are 18; things inside a container are 12; marks are 6; Wrapped and share cards are 28. Concentric: inner = outer minus padding (18 - 6 = 12). card is the radius of the 1600px export, separate from the scale. borderCurve continuous on every rounded rectangle.

shadow._comment: Exactly one, for things that float over content: a dragged Wrapped card, a toast. Nothing in the scroll flow has a shadow. No coloured glows, including under the primary button.

_comment: The 1-bit texture: Wrapped headers, the archetype hero, empty-state art, dithered data.
cell is the grain in points (3pt = 9 device pixels at @3x, so it lands on whole pixels).
bayer8 is the ordered-dither threshold table, row-major, 0..63; a cell is ink when its
value v (0..1) is STRICTLY greater than bayer8/64, so white stays paper. The SkSL computes
it arithmetically (no dynamic array indexing in SkSL); gen_tokens.py asserts the table and
the arithmetic agree, and the phone's test asserts the TypeScript port against the table.
Nine identity hues: creatures, sessions, Wrapped cards, harness tiles, archetypes and the
five dimensions. Never chrome (tab bar, buttons other than the amber primary, rows, screens),
never a pale fill with a same hue border and text, never a gradient, never at partial opacity
over the ground. design-refs/DESIGN-V2-COLOUR-MOTION.md section 1 has every measurement.
dark          the ink on the dark ground: marks, creatures, hue labels, and a solid fill with
surface.text.light on it. 4.5:1 or more on bg and card; ink on it 4.5:1 or more.
partner       the dither's middle tone (paper, partner, ink) and nothing else: never text, never
a creature on its own. 3:1 on card, 1.5 to 2.6:1 below its ink, chroma kept.
light         the mark tone on the light ground (a creature, a glyph, a ring): 3:1 on #FBF9F5.
lightText     the hue as text on the light ground: 4.5:1 on #FBF9F5 and on white.
lightPartner  the light appearance's middle tone, between paper and the mark tone.
gen_tokens.py refuses a hue under any of those floors, an identity ink inside the bands data
owns (OKLCH hue 19 to 42: del and Claude's terracotta; 120 to 200: add and the human teal),
two inks closer than 0.10 in OKLab, and a mapping that names a hue that does not exist.

creature._comment: One ink per creature. Bit is the brand, so Bit is amber; the eight animals never are.

_comment: A session's creature: ring[fnv1a32(client_session_id) % 8], stepped forward along the ring
past any creature a session running at its start already wears. Never Bit, so no session is
ever amber: on a live surface amber means 'needs you' and nothing else. Warm and cool
alternate, so a stepped session lands on a hue far from the one it stepped past.

harness._comment: Where the harness is the object (the picker, the Stack page, Settings). Never the vendor's colour, never amber. Keyed by HARNESS_MARKS id: cursor_ide and cursor_agent are the one cursor mark.

card._comment: The fifteen Wrapped cards, in wrapped.CARD_IDS order. builder_type wears the archetype's hue; no card meets its own hue across (i+1) or down the two column grid (i+2), whichever hue card one wears (cardAlt), which gen_tokens.py checks.

cardAlt._comment: What card 2 or 3 wears when the archetype's hue is already its own.

archetype._comment: The archetype's creature's hue (pixel/animals.ts ARCHETYPE_ANIMALS and CORPUS_ARCHETYPE_ANIMALS; bun test holds the two equal). The generalist is Bit's amber.

dimension._comment: Each dimension wears the hue of the archetype whose rule reads it (analysis/profile.py ARCHETYPE_RULES): steer_rate is the skeptic's, code_velocity the velocity machine's, test runs the quality guardian's, planning_ratio the architect's. No rule reads product instinct; it takes the director's cobalt, the archetype about pointing the work.

verdict._comment: State colours, not identity: a token path. Circling is textDim, so the neutral verdict is never the loudest word on a tile.

card._comment: 1600x900 is the X landscape shape; 1080x1350 is the 4:5 portrait shape. Rendered @2x.
